elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the operative subject is "each Party", so the cap binds both Array and Ono. Nothing retained states that either Party's liability is unlimited (16.5 is a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer only).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Basis is "fees paid or payable" (not broader "all amounts"), lookback is anchored to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present. Caveat noted in reasons: "fees" is undefined in this license, whose consideration is upfront, milestone and royalty payments.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — already mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations..." and the cap opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include "its data protection or security obligations".

Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2" — the same indemnity set already identified as the Agreement's indemnities in retained 16.5, so the carve-out reaches all indemnification obligations in the document.
Excluded Claims include "its gross negligence"; consistent with the retained 16.5 proviso disapplying the limitation for gross negligence.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights."

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims and Ono's payment obligations under this Agreement, which are excluded from the damages subject to this cap..." Ono is the licensee/paying Party (Customer-side alias), and the carve-out covers its payment obligations as a whole, not a narrow subset of a defined fee. The deterministic check flagged this only because the drafted text uses the party name "Ono" rather than the literal token "Customer"; in substance the element is satisfied.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 16.7 caps "each Party's total aggregate liability".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 floor).
Excluded Claims include indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include breach of confidentiality obligations.

reasons: Finding classification is sound: Article 16 contains only a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer and no aggregate monetary cap, so the clause fails the fallback element requiring a mutual 12-months-fees cap; a redline is warranted.

All eleven preferred elements are met by the single inserted Section 16.7 plus the retained mutual disclaimer in 16.5, so the position is complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

The deterministic 'preferred payment carve-out covers Customer payment obligations' failure is a naming artefact only: the clause carves out 'Ono's payment obligations under this Agreement' in full, and Ono is the customer-side Party under the alias list. No repair needed, though substituting a defined reference (e.g. 'Ono's payment obligations under Article 8') would remove any doubt.

Minimality holds: one concise new section is inserted, no existing wording is deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category is added. The only borderline surplus is the appositive 'which are excluded from the damages subject to this cap', which merely restates the 'Except for' operator; it could be deleted without loss.

Intent is preserved: 16.5 and its indemnity/gross-negligence provisos survive without contradiction (the new Excluded Claims definition tracks the same Article 10 / 16.1 / 16.2 indemnities), and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting defect to repair before sending: 'fees' is undefined and does not match this Agreement's consideration structure (upfront, milestone and royalty payments). A counterparty could argue royalties and milestones are not 'fees', leaving USD 1,000,000 as the effective cap. Tie the basis expressly to amounts payable by Ono under Article 8 (or 'all amounts paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement' if we are willing to move off the playbook wording).

Placement check: the insertion is anchored after an unrelated recall paragraph (p0733). Confirm the new section physically sits within Article 16 after 16.5/16.6 and that '16.7' does not collide with an existing subsection number.

Commercial caution to raise with the deal team before tabling: both Parties are currently uncapped, so imposing a USD 1,000,000 / 12-months-fees cap also caps Ono's recovery against Array in a licence with far larger milestone and royalty exposure. Confirm the floor is adequate, or propose a materially higher fixed floor keyed to amounts paid under Article 8.
